objective_for_doctor: A 61-year-old F patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve been having pain around my mouth, forehead, right cheek, and nose, with a burning and sharp feeling. My fever is also present, and I’ve had a cold in the last 2 weeks along with a cough and greenish or yellowish nasal discharge.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—can you tell me: do you have any blisters or sores around your mouth/nose, and is the facial pain one-sided (right) or both sides?  
Doctor: Also, do you have any eye symptoms (redness, pain, vision changes) or swelling around the eye/cheek?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CBC + CRP; REQUEST TEST: Sinus CT (or CT orbits/sinuses if available)

I don’t know.  

The facial pain is around my mouth, forehead, right cheek, and nose—so it’s on the right side (at least for the cheek).  

I don’t know about any eye symptoms or swelling around the eye/cheek.

Doctor: I’m going to ask a few targeted questions—first, is the pain worse when you bend forward or when you press over your right cheek/sinuses?  
Doctor: Second, did you notice any new rash or tiny fluid-filled blisters on the right side of your face around the nose/mouth (even if mild)?  
Doctor: Third, how high is your fever (or highest temp), and how long has it been going on?

Yes—the pain is worse when you press over my right cheek/sinuses.

I don’t know about any new rash or tiny fluid-filled blisters on the right side of my face around the nose/mouth.

I don’t know how high my fever was (or the highest temperature). I’ve had the cold in the last 2 weeks, along with the cough and greenish or yellowish nasal discharge.

Doctor: Thanks—next question: do you have foul-smelling nasal discharge or worsening facial pressure after the cold (i.e., did symptoms “improve then worsen”)?  
Doctor: Also, any tooth pain on the right upper teeth or pain when chewing?

I don’t know about foul-smelling nasal discharge or worsening facial pressure after the cold.

I don’t know about tooth pain on the right upper teeth or pain when chewing.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—given the right-sided cheek/forehead/nose pain that’s worse with pressure and your recent 2-week cold with green/yellow discharge, I suspect a sinus infection; can you tell me: do you have reduced sense of smell or thick post-nasal drip, and is your fever currently high again?  
Doctor: Also, do you have any severe headache, neck stiffness, confusion, or trouble seeing/moving your eye?  
Doctor: If you can, I’ll order results now—REQUEST TEST: Basic Metabolic Panel + COVID/Influenza test.
Yes—I’ve lost my sense of smell.

Doctor: Lost smell with persistent right-sided facial pain worse on pressure after a 2-week cold strongly suggests acute rhinosinusitis; are you having any severe headache or visual changes, or swelling/redness around the right eye?  
Doctor: If no, I’ll proceed—REQUEST TEST: Sinus evaluation/CT (if not already), and review CBC+CRP results for severity.

No severe headache, neck stiffness, confusion, or trouble seeing/moving my eye.

I don’t know about swelling/redness around the right eye.

Doctor: Given your loss of smell, persistent right-sided facial pain worse with pressure, and recent 2-week cold with yellow/green discharge—plus no eye-threatening neurologic symptoms—this fits acute bacterial rhinosinusitis; I need one last check: are you immunocompromised (e.g., diabetes, steroids), and how long have symptoms been at least 10 days without improving or did they worsen again after initial improvement?  
Doctor: If you can’t recall, I’ll treat as bacterial and ask: any current severe facial swelling or worsening despite over-the-counter measures?  
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute bacterial rhinosinusitis (right-sided), likely rhinosinusitis after viral URI with anosmia.
